title: Final-retry Newton iteration-prefix tomography across G21H adjacent status boundaries
bounded_conclusions: Iteration-prefix tomography reproduces the complete G21H final-retry classification for all four frozen heads without changing production HeadCalc or solver state.

At B1, the adjacent status-6 and status-0 heads have identical cumulative backtracking counts [1,2,5,8] through iteration 4; the status-0 head converges at iteration 4 while the status-6 head does not.
At B2, the adjacent heads have identical cumulative backtracking counts [1,2,3] through iteration 3; the status-0 head converges at iteration 3 while the status-6 head does not.

Therefore the adjacent-head status bifurcation is not preceded by an observable difference in backtracking-count trajectory up to the successful side's convergence point. The causal branch is localized to the convergence decision after an otherwise count-equivalent Newton/backtracking prefix, or to numerical state differences inside that prefix not represented by the aggregate backtracking count.
After the split, the status-6 trajectories continue and eventually saturate at much larger backtracking work: 104 attempts for B1 and 39 for B2 at iteration 16.

The next diagnostic must decompose the exact HeadCalc convergence criteria at the split iteration: compartment balance, head-change, total balance and any ponding criterion. A deeper Newton-state trace is only needed if those criteria do not localize the branch.
No solver tolerance, retry policy, participant acceptance rule, status smoothing, response-space globalization policy or production HCOF/RHS behavior is changed or admitted.
next_natural_unit: Open G21J as convergence-criterion forensics at B1 iteration 4 and B2 iteration 3. Obtain read-only end-of-iteration criterion diagnostics for the adjacent status-6/status-0 heads and identify which HeadCalc convergence predicate flips. Keep production HeadCalc byte-unchanged if a test-only observational seam can expose the needed scratch safely.
